draft.title: How moving water changes places
card: Moving water links places. Water that falls in the hills flows downstream and reaches towns and farms far away.
It also carries soil and small pieces of rock downstream. These are dropped where the water slows down.
Moving water erodes, which means it wears away rock and soil. Over a long time, it can cut valleys and shape the land.
Fast water can erode and carry more than slow water. A swollen river after heavy rain can change its banks quickly.
draft.remember: Moving water joins places together and wears away land as it flows.

a.q: What does it mean when a river erodes its banks?
opts: It wears away the soil and rock of the banks
It drops soil and rock along the banks
It stores water in the soil of the banks
It joins the banks to a nearby lake
a.why: Erosion is the wearing away of rock and soil by moving water. Dropping soil is tempting, but that happens when water slows down, and it is not erosion.
a.clue: Erosion takes material away from the land.

b.q: A creek in the Northern Territory flows fast after a storm and the water turns brown. What best explains the brown colour?
opts: The water is carrying soil it has worn from the land
The water is bringing new soil up from the sea
The water is soaking into the soil of the banks
The water is slowing down and dropping its soil
b.why: Fast water erodes soil and carries it downstream, which makes the water look brown. Dropping soil is tempting, but that happens when water slows, and the creek is flowing fast.
b.clue: Think about what fast water picks up and carries.

a.best: It wears away the soil and rock of the banks

b.best: The water is carrying soil it has worn from the land
